item.title: Levenshtein-type bounds for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal $s$-codes and for minimal energy) for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid $(a,b)$. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials). Under these hypotheses and suitable node-location assumptions, the resulting cardinality bounds are optimal within the corresponding degree restriction and unique under natural nondegeneracy conditions. Under proper conditions on the quadrature nodes, we obtain universal lower energy bounds by utilizing Hermite interpolants as polynomial solutions of the respective linear program. Common test functions characterize optimality in the full polynomial linear programs under mild additional assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Peter Dragnev, Peter Grabner

item.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.08809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.
item.dc:creator: Xin Xiong, Mathew Salas, Sihua Shao, Chen Chen, Mostafa Hassanalian, Rafael Fierro

item.title: The Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. In this paper, we aim to study the parameters of the Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances $\delta_{1}$ and $\delta_{2}$, respectively, where $2\le \delta_{1},\delta_{2}\le n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2$ be the Schur product of $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$. We present some necessary and sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2\ne\mathbb{F}_q^n$ by applying some constraints to $\delta_{1}$ and $\delta_{2}$. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.
item.dc:creator: Haojie Xu, Xia Wu, Wei Lu, Xiwang Cao

item.title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.08982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Akrout

item.title: Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.
item.dc:creator: Tofar C. -Y. Chang, I-Hsiang Lee, Pin-Han Wang, Jian-Jia Weng, Yu T. Su

item.title: Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage
item.description: arXiv:2611.09366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a decoding algorithm for a Reed--Solomon product code targeted at the demanding reliability requirements of modern magnetic tape storage. For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Chvanov, Nikolay Malkovsky

item.title: Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2611.09383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. For energies proportional to block length, an additional gain condition ensures that this exponent is at least that of the total-energy spherical ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Nir Elkayam, Meir Feder

item.title: Symmetry Breaking over Multiway Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.09466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identical users running the same algorithm must often break their symmetry and agree on distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation. We study anonymous symmetry breaking over a discrete memoryless multiway channel invariant under permutations of its $J$ users: each user observes only a private output and must choose a number in $\{1,\dots,J\}$, and the symmetry is broken if the $J$ numbers are distinct. Using a R\'enyi change of measure, we derive a finite-blocklength converse on the error probability of every symmetric causal protocol, including adaptive and randomized ones. For achievability, block coding with random names reduces the problem to all-source multicast, for which we derive a Gallager random-coding exponent for every fixed $J$, and a cut-set bound that limits the exponent of the probability that two names coincide or are decoded wrongly. Interactive role controllers instead let the users contend for identifiers directly: we give their exact error probability, an achievable exponent given by a spectral radius when some outputs certify a role, and a floor for finite-state controllers when every output has positive probability, and we introduce generalized musical chairs. On a noisy bandit channel motivated by multiplayer multi-armed bandits, with noiseless collisions and arms of a common mean below one, interactive schemes provably exceed the limit of name decoding, and numerical estimates suggest the same with noisy collisions. For two users, noiseless collisions, one informative arm and a silent arm, the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhang, Richard Combes, Sheng Yang

item.title: Capacity of Generic Symmetric Distributed Linear Computation: The Geometry of Relations
item.description:
arXiv:2611.09636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In distributed linear computation, $K$ users observe linear functions of common finite-field data and send separate messages to a server that wants another linear function. We characterize the generic capacity $C$, the minimum total number of field symbols sent per computed instance, when all observations and the demand have dimension $
u$, the data have dimension $\mu$, and the coefficients of these linear functions are drawn independently and uniformly from the field and stay fixed during coding, with the field size growing through arbitrary prime powers. For fixed $K$, $C/
u$ depends only on $	au=\mu/
u$: the curve has finitely many linear pieces for at most three users, infinitely many pieces approaching one value of $	au$ for four users, and a rational part between two sequences of linear pieces for five or more users. The geometry of the relation space, formed by the linear relations among the observations and the demand, determines three things: the shape of the curve, which relations the coding scheme aligns, and the entropy inequalities used in the converse. Generically, the user subspaces of this space are either balanced, where the capacity lies on a single rational curve, or split into two balanced components, a sparse and a dense one, which produces the linear pieces. Achievability uses asymptotic set alignment, in which monomial precoders confine the combined observation differences to a small set. The converse uses the same geometry to lower-bound the sum of the users' remaining observation entropies in terms of the remaining data entropy.
item.dc:creator: Hua Sun

item.title: An Efficient Synchronization Scheme for Distributed Bandits
item.description: arXiv:2611.09806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. Finally, applying these results to distributed multi-armed bandits, we show an upper bound on the regret of our synchronization scheme.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhang, Henrique Miyamoto, Richard Combes, Sheng Yang

item.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Data Deduplication Under a Constant Edit Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data deduplication has become increasingly important in large-scale storage systems, driven by the rapid growth of digital data. By identifying and removing repeats in the data stream, deduplication saves storage space more efficiently than traditional compression methods. In this paper, we study the performance of variable-length deduplication and multi-chunk deduplication algorithms from an information-theoretic perspective, focusing on data streams where repeats are approximate rather than exact. We consider two probabilistic source models in which source strings consist of repeated blocks that are modified by either a constant number of substitution edits or burst-insertion edits per block, the latter capturing the localized edit patterns commonly observed in real-world data. For both models, we show that variable-length deduplication achieves asymptotically arbitrarily large compression ratios, and that multi-chunk deduplication achieves compression within a constant factor of the source entropy under mild conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sarvin Motamen, Hao Lou, Farzad Farnoud

item.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
item.description: arXiv:2611.09848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain? We answer with one pre-registered run on 1,000 English user utterances from Taskmaster-1. The primary endpoint is the cost per message to deliver 100% of the messages (hash bits, plus a 2-byte negative acknowledgement and the raw text when the first attempt fails), paired against an in-domain PPM order-1 sender. The hash-only sender delivered 857 of 1,000 messages on the first attempt and cost 192.8 bits per message, 18.4 bits more than PPM order 1 (95% bootstrap interval 10.9 to 26.3); by the pre-registered rule it spends more and is not equivalent within one byte. As secondary results we map measured sender memory against bits. The hash-only sender (8,190 B on a host build, keyed BLAKE2b tag included, as in every method) was the cheapest point in bits from 8,190 B up to, but excluding, PPM order 1 at 24,844 B, 45 to 46 bits below smaz2 and Unishox2; from PPM order 1 upwards, in-domain senders spend fewer bits, except order 2 pruned to 16 KiB. In airtime it loses to PPM order 1 on all five links priced, to Unishox2 on four, and to raw text with a tag on two, because each failure costs an acknowledgement frame and a fallback frame. A wider receiver search recovers half of the failures and makes the cost 7.7 bits lower than PPM order 1, at about three minutes of receiver time per failure, and still loses in airtime on four of five links. We report the measurement as a delimitation, with every deviation of the run.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Samoilenko

item.title: Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$. For these codes the stable profile is equivalent to minimality with the largest possible minimum distance; for even $m$ the analogous class consists of minimal MRD codes. More generally, for $1\le\tau\le m-2$ and $\gcd(m,\tau+1)=1$, we obtain nondegenerate $\tau$-minimal codes of length $(\tau+1)K$ for every sufficiently large $K$, uniformly in $q$. We also construct maximum $h$-designs whose number of members grows exponentially with the ambient dimension at fixed $q,n,h$, and the associated maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes with a growing number of equal long blocks. In extension degree five, the ordinary and $2$-minimal constructions hold for every $q$ and every $K\ge32$ and $K\ge59$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Giannoni

item.title: A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finding exact solutions for the statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms (CGQFs) has long been a challenging problem. Among existing exact approaches, Raphaeli's formulation [1] remains the most computationally efficient. However, its analytical tractability is hindered by the dependence of its series coefficients on the evaluation variable, which confines their statistics to the probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF). This paper overcomes this limitation by deriving novel Gamma-mixture representations for the PDF and CDF of positive- and negative-definite noncentral CGQFs. The resulting structure broadens Raphaeli's statistical framework beyond the PDF and CDF to a wider class of CGQF functionals and a substantial range of practical applications. In particular, expectations of integrable functions of definite noncentral CGQFs are expressed as weighted sums of the corresponding expectations over Gamma random variables, enabling the direct derivation of moments, transforms, and performance measures. Moreover, the proposed formulation reduces the single-point complexity from \(O\!\left(n^2K+nK^2\right)\) for Raphaeli's method to \(O\!\left(nK+K^2\right)\), where \(n\) denotes the quadratic-form dimension and \(K\) the truncation order. The proposed Gamma-mixture structure also enables closed-form approximations that, by construction, remain valid probability distributions for any truncation order. In addition, uniform PDF and CDF truncation-error bounds are derived, allowing prescribed-accuracy truncation. As a sample application, we derive the first reported exact average bit error rate expression for maximal-ratio combining receivers with an arbitrary number of branches under an arbitrary positive-definite Rician correlation structure.
item.dc:creator: Fernando D. Almeida Garc\'ia, Carlos R. Nogueira da Silva, Felipe A. P. de Figueiredo, Rausley A. A. de Souza, Michel Daoud Yacoub, Jos\'e C\^andido Silveira Santos Filho

item.title: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
item.description: arXiv:2611.08783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. To reduce communication delay, we utilize multi-antenna beamforming and propose a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) uplink transmission and aggregation method for simultaneous training of multiple models. Devices are formed into groups for local model training based on the model assignments per communication round and simultaneously perform OTA aggregation over a multi-access channel. Based on the M-OTA transmission and reception process, we formulate a joint optimization of transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping over $T$ communication rounds to maximize the training convergence rates of all models. We analyze the per-model optimality gap, which captures the impact of noisy aggregation and inter-model interference on the learning performance. We further show that the $T$-round joint optimization problem can be decomposed into per-round online optimization to devise solutions. Following this, we propose a device grouping strategy that explores channel correlation among devices to maximize OTA aggregation performance. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity iterative algorithm for joint transmit-receive beamforming with closed-form updates. Simulation shows that our proposed M-OTA approach substantially outperforms the conventional single-model sequential OTA approach and other commonly used beamforming schemes.
item.dc:creator: Chong Zhang, Min Dong, Ben Liang, Ali Afana, Yahia A. Eldemerdash Ahmed

item.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
item.description: arXiv:2611.09183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $\epsilon$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $\epsilon$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/\epsilon$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set.In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(\epsilon)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/\epsilon^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.
item.dc:creator: Prahladh Harsha, Swastik Kopparty, Mrinal Kumar, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Madhu Sudan

item.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $\rho>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $\rho$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Dobson, Varun Jog, Chun Hei Michael Shiu

item.title: Orders between channels and implications for partial information decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2305.06021v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The partial information decomposition (PID) framework is concerned with decomposing the information that a set of random variables has with respect to a target variable into three types of components: redundant, synergistic, and unique. Classical information theory alone does not provide a unique way to decompose information in this manner and additional assumptions have to be made. Recently, Kolchinsky proposed a new general axiomatic approach to obtain measures of redundant information, based on choosing a preorder relation between information sources (equivalently, a preorder between communication channels). In this paper, we exploit this approach to introduce three new measures of redundant information (and the resulting decompositions) based on well-known preorders between channels, thus contributing to the enrichment of the PID landscape. We relate the new decompositions to existing ones, study some of their properties, and provide examples illustrating their novelty. As a side result, we prove that any preorder that satisfies Kolchinsky's axioms yields a decomposition that meets the axioms originally introduced by Williams and Beer when they first propose the PID.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e F. C. Gomes, M\'ario A. T. Figueiredo

item.title: A Two-Term Ziv-Zakai Bound for Multitarget DoA Estimation in MIMO Radar
item.description: arXiv:2511.08326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multitarget direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is challenging when fluctuating targets are closely spaced: local Cram\'er--Rao bounds (CRBs) miss global errors, while direct vector Ziv--Zakai bound (ZZB) evaluation is computationally demanding. For colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with Swerling-II fluctuations and an ordered angular prior, we derive a rigorous two-term Bayesian mean squared error lower bound. A finite separation contribution addresses nonlocal discrimination, while a correction based on the prior averaged Fisher information matrix (FIM) retains target coupling and virtual array geometry. We show that the prior averaged pointwise CRB diverges under unrestricted target spacing when the FIM is nonsingular almost everywhere, although the proposed bound remains finite. Once the averaged FIM is obtained, evaluation avoids displacement optimization and multidimensional binary error integration. The bound supports analysis of snapshot diversity, target spacing, and transmit and receive allocation. Numerical comparison with the vector ZZB shows close agreement at low SNR but greater conservatism at high SNR, quantifying the tradeoff in tightness.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Bakhshizadeh Mohajer, Daniela Tuninetti, Luca Barletta

item.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2606.11987v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.
item.dc:creator: Ragnar Freij-Hollanti, Kirsten D. Morris, Patricija \v{S}apokait\.e

item.title: Sharp Minimax Regret for Infinite-Memory Logistic Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2608.26515v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sequential prediction of binary marks whose log-odds are a linear function of all past inputs. The inputs are independent uniform signs. The coefficient of the input observed $j$ steps earlier is unknown, but its absolute value is at most a known number $r_j$, and $\sum_j r_j\le B$. A learner is judged by its expected cumulative log loss in excess of the loss of the true conditional probabilities. We show that for every such sequence $r$ and every horizon $T$, the minimax value of this regret lies between $c\,\Gamma_T(r)/\max\{1,B^2\}$ and $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$, where $\Gamma_T(r)=\sum_{j\le T}\log(1+(T-j+1)r_j^2)$ and $c$ is an absolute constant. The term for lag $j$ combines the size bound $r_j$ with the number $T-j+1$ of rounds in which that lag influences a prediction, and no monotonicity or other regularity of $r$ is needed. The upper bound is attained by a Bayesian mixture with independent Gaussian priors. For the lower bound, we apply the van Trees inequality at each prediction step and then bound the expected log-determinant of the random matrix whose rows are the lagged input vectors. We also characterize when $\frac12$ is the exact leading constant: for envelopes with a common bound $B$, possibly changing with $T$, the regret is asymptotic to $\frac12\Gamma_T(r)$ if and only if $\sum_{j\le T}\min\{1,(T-j+1)r_j^2\}=o(\Gamma_T(r))$. This gives, for example, $\log^2(A^2T)/(8\alpha)$ for $r_j=Ae^{-\alpha j}$, whereas for $r_j=Aj^{-s}$ with $s>1$ the regret is of order $T^{1/(2s)}$ and its ratio to $\Gamma_T(r)$ stays below $\frac12$. Finally, for a known horizon, an online Newton predictor with features scaled by $r_j$ attains regret of order $\Gamma_T(r)$ with polynomial computation per round.
item.dc:creator: Vaneet Aggarwal

item.title: The Gaussian Multiuser Channel Capacity Region
item.description: arXiv:2609.17212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work characterizes a Gaussian multiuser-channel capacity-region using receiver-subset message atoms, Gaussian single-user equivalents, and successive decoding. A memoryless multiuser-channel model specifies both the channel conditional distribution and the independent-use input distribution. For all linear Gaussian channels, independent Gaussian user signaling and receiver-local worst-case-noise/MMSE-GDFE transformations provide a single-user-equivalent basis for the complete capacity-region construction. Each user distributes its input autocorrelation among a finite set of receiver-subset atoms, whose rate sums satisfy the applicable receiver constraints. Minimum-energy and weighted-rate-sum designs optimize these allocations, while fixed-allocation linear programs determine feasible atomic rates and synchronized time-shared successive-decoding implementations. The resulting framework includes Gaussian multiple-access, broadcast, and interference channels, with numerical examples illustrating their rate regions and receiver designs.
item.dc:creator: John M. Cioffi

item.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.25490v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.
item.dc:creator: Chao Tian, Krishna Narayanan

item.title: Landscape Analysis of Simultaneous Blind Deconvolution and Phase Retrieval via Structured Low-Rank Tensor Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2509.10834v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the landscape of the simultaneous blind deconvolution and phase retrieval (BDPR) problem via a structured low-rank tensor recovery framework. Since the complicated sensing structure makes direct landscape analysis technically challenging, we introduce a tractable tensor sensing surrogate that preserves the essential low-rank structure. We first analyze its population risk, characterize the global landscape on the unit sphere, and establish local linear convergence of Riemannian gradient descent (RGD) under mild conditions. We then extend the analysis to tensor sensing under a tensor restricted isometry property (TRIP), establishing local geometric and RGD convergence guarantees, and quantify robustness to measurement noise. Our theoretical results are further supported by extensive numerical experiments. These findings offer insights into the optimization landscape of the surrogate tensor sensing problem, thereby providing guidance for studying and solving the original BDPR problem.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Liang, Zhen Qin, Zhihui Zhu, Shuang Li

item.title: Fast Statistical Rates for Flow Matching without Curvature Assumptions
item.description: arXiv:2601.20250v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Flow-based generative models have emerged as an efficient alternative to diffusion models. We study the sample complexity of learning a target distribution in Wasserstein distance via flow matching, which learns a velocity field transporting a base distribution to the target. Under exact empirical risk minimization over a fixed network class and standard assumptions on the architecture and data distribution, we show that any squared-loss flow-matching variant including rectified flow with bounded derivatives achieves $\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sample complexity for the statistical term with the Wasserstein guarantee taking the form $W_2 \le K(\varepsilon + C\varepsilon_{app})$, where $\varepsilon_{app}$ is the approximation error of the network class. This improves upon existing $\widetilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ guarantees and does not require the Polyak--Lojasiewicz condition in the statistical analysis. Instead, we exploit a structural property of the squared-loss objective - it induces an approximate Bernstein condition that directly ties the variance of the excess loss to the excess risk up to additive approximation-error. This condition enables a localized Rademacher complexity analysis yielding fast $O(1/n)$ rates. The flow-matching schedule enters the leading statistical prefactor through the Lipschitz constant of the pointwise loss, which we characterize explicitly for standard schedules.
item.dc:creator: Hari Krishna Sahoo, Mudit Gaur, Vaneet Aggarwal

item.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2603.09722v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Li, Wengu Chen, Huanmin Ge, Dachun Yang

item.title: AirFM-DDA: Air-Interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle Domain for AI-Native 6G
item.description: arXiv:2605.00020v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The success of large foundation models is catalyzing a new paradigm for AI-native 6G network design: wireless foundation models for physical-layer design. However, existing models often operate on channel state information (CSI) in the spatial-temporal-frequency (STF) domain, where multipath components are superimposed and structurally entangled. This hinders the learning of a universal channel representation. Their reliance on global attention also incurs prohibitive overhead. In this paper, we propose AirFM-DDA, an Air-interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle (DDA) domain. AirFM-DDA reparameterizes CSI into the DDA domain to resolve multipath components along physically meaningful axes and employs window-based attention with frame-structure-aware positional encoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate transferability across scenarios, tasks, datasets, and antenna configurations. For channel prediction and estimation, AirFM-DDA generalizes zero-shot to unseen cities, achieving average normalized mean-square error (NMSE) gains of 4.9-8.5 dB over the strongest baselines. With only 10% labeled data, it achieves average gains of 12.0 percentage points in Top-1 accuracy for beam prediction and 3.4 percentage points in F1 score for line-of-sight (LoS) identification. It further transfers across simulated datasets and adapts to measured data and different antenna arrays. Compared with global attention, window-based attention reduces training and inference costs by nearly an order of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Kejia Bian, Meixia Tao, Jianhua Mo, Zhiyong Chen, Leyan Chen

item.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
item.description: arXiv:2605.23362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over na\"ive uniform allocation.
item.dc:creator: Junghyun Lee, Sanghwa Kim, Yassir Jedra, Alexandre Prouti\`ere, Se-Young Yun

item.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.36727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and linearized polynomials connect field extensions, normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Cyclotomic cosets link additive symmetries and local phase data with polynomial composition, factorization, and compatible lifting. Low-degree subfield representations and relative traces lead to root-block recovery, while return maps on root fibers organize constructions of irreducible polynomials. Coding applications include duality, distance bounds, Fourier support, and syndrome decoding. Character sums yield trace-norm distributions, the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field sums and curve point counts. The final chapter constructs finite fields as residue fields of unramified p-adic extensions and relates Teichmuller representatives and Hensel lifting to cyclotomic orbits, periodic digit expansions, Witt carries, coefficient valuations, and Newton slopes. The emphasis throughout is on explicit proofs and reusable connections between field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hongfeng Wu, Li Zhu

item.title: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
item.description: arXiv:2611.04678v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending the result of [GGS26] to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. Namely, we show that any $q$-query RLDC $C\colon \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^n$ must satisfy $n = k^{1+\Omega(1/q)}$, closely matching the upper bound of $n = k^{1+O(1/q)}$ by Ben-Sasson, Goldreich, Harsha, Sudan, and Vadhan (STOC 2004). Our proof reduces showing RLDC lower bounds to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders. To this end, we introduce a capped Horvitz--Thompson estimator with uniformly bounded discrete derivatives on the $p$-biased cube. We establish its concentration of measure via self-bounding inequalities and control the downward bias induced by capping through a spreadness argument.
